No actionable introduced defect was found, and the maintainer explicitly disposed of the previous upgrade-proof request. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `afe7cd506d9bac34615d686419b33e22a06eb063` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent runtime repair with meaningful boundary evidence and no actionable findings; the upgrade-proof exception remains explicit. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The captured evidence exercises production admission with real SQLite children and HTTP, observing healthy service during refusal, guarded recovery, revoked-write rejection, and shutdown drainage. It supports this internal runtime repair; the expressly skipped updater and Windows-service scenarios are not claimed as passing. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The captured evidence exercises production admission with real SQLite children and HTTP, observing healthy service during refusal, guarded recovery, revoked-write rejection, and shutdown drainage. It supports this internal runtime repair; the expressly skipped updater and Windows-service scenarios are not claimed as passing. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Current main still lacks deferred admission: Fetched main awaits all scheduled inspections and propagates their failures; it has no foreground-to-background handoff. Earlier merged budget and reader-reuse improvements therefore do not supersede this repair.
Deferred admission retains live ownership checks: Recovery checks cancellation, the pending refusal, deletion state, and file identity, rejects incompatible or migration-required results, and delegates preparation before clearing admission.
Preparation and publication use existing owners: The Gateway verifies configured database paths, guards secrets publication against configuration and revision changes, restricts session preparation to the deferred agent, and requires a current model snapshot. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Gateway startup checks each agent’s SQLite database before allowing session access. This change transfers unfinished checks into the Gateway lifetime while keeping affected agents unavailable until preparation succeeds. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Configured agent databases] --> B[Bounded startup inspections] B --> C[Healthy agents serve] B --> D[Deferred agent stays degraded] D --> E[Background inspection] E --> F[Guarded credential and session preparation] F --> G[Publish models and readmit agent] H[Gateway shutdown] --> E H --> F ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Gateway liveness can succeed while an existing agent remains unavailable; deferred databases requiring migration remain degraded until Doctor repair. Published-updater and retained Windows-supervisor compatibility remain unproven under the recorded scoped exception. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150574 Summary: This PR is the active implementation candidate for the reported fatal slow-database startup path. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150574 - The PR explicitly targets this report's healthy-database startup timeout. - `superseded`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150677 - The captured discussion identifies the closed-unmerged PR as the replaced submission for the same branch and change. - `partial_overlap`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150444 - The merged reader-reuse optimization addresses inspection overhead but leaves fatal timeout handling in place. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150564 - The merged Linux spawn broker supplies a lifecycle boundary composed by this PR, rather than the same startup-timeout repair. Yes: separating the foreground wait from inspection cancellation preserves integrity checks and reuses existing preparation owners without adding configuration or a competing scheduler. Inspected tests exercise those production owners; the canonical-validation regression revokes authority before worker write admission and requires pending validation to remain. These checks were inspected, not rerun.
